why: The trait every board crate's own config struct implements, exposing the two fields that are universal across boards -- `locator()` and `domain_id()`. Board configs are otherwise wildly board-specific (MAC, static IP, gateway, UART base, WiFi SSID), so cross-board generic code -- a benchmark harness, a multi-target test driver -- had to `cfg`-gate on the concrete type name to read even those two. rclrs has nothing to correlate against because a desktop node has no board: the transport endpoint comes from the middleware's own config file and the domain from the environment. Anchors `BoardConfig::*`; `zenoh_locator` is argued separately. The transport-specific knobs stay ordinary fields on the concrete struct, written by the DEPLOY OVERLAY (`BoardEntry::run_with_deploy`), so this trait stays two methods wide on purpose. A `BoardTransportConfig` trait of mutable setters existed until issue 1064 removed it: five boards implemented it and nothing ever called it.
